Q7842461.label: 1981 Trinidad and Tobago general election
Q7842461.desc: general election in Trinidad and Tobago
Q7842461.summary: General elections were held in Trinidad and Tobago on 9 November 1981. The result was a victory for the People's National Movement, which won 26 of the 36 seats. Voter turnout was 56.4%.

Q108908701.label: 2021 Barbadian presidential election
Q108908701.summary: The 2021 Barbadian presidential election was held on 20 October 2021 to choose the first president of Barbados, an office established as part of Barbados becoming a republic.

Q3562653.label: 1944 Guatemalan presidential election
Q3562653.summary: Presidential elections were held in Guatemala between 17 and 19 December 1944. The October Revolution had overthrown Jorge Ubico, the American-backed dictator, after which a junta composed of Francisco Javier Arana, Jacobo Árbenz and Jorge Toriello took power, and quickly announced presidential elections, as well as elections for a constitutional assembly. The subsequent elections were broadly considered free and fair, although only literate men were given the vote. Unlike in similar historical situations, none of the junta members stood for election.

Q5174941.label: 1930 Costa Rican parliamentary election
Q5174941.summary: Mid-term parliamentary elections were held in Costa Rica on 9 February 1930. The result was a victory for the National Union Party, which received 33% of the vote. Voter turnout was 31%.

mentions.c: Costa Rica: 1930 Costa Rican parliamentary election

Q1630365.label: Democratic Revolutionary Party
Q1630365.summary: The Democratic Revolutionary Party is a centre-left political party in Panama founded in 1979 by General Omar Torrijos. To date, it has been the party of four Panamian presidents: Nicolás Ardito Barletta Vallarino (1984–1985), Ernesto Pérez Balladares (1994–1999), Martin Torrijos (2004–2009) and Laurentino Cortizo (2019–2024).

Q42733725.label: 2021 Dutch general election
Q42733725.desc: general election held in the Netherlands
Q42733725.summary: General elections were held in the Netherlands from 15 to 17 March 2021 to elect all 150 members of the House of Representatives. Following the elections and lengthy coalition formation talks, the sitting government remained in power.

Q2532509.label: Belgian Socialist Party
Q2532509.summary: The Belgian Socialist Party was a social-democratic political party which existed in Belgium from 1945 to 1978. During its time in office, a number of progressive social reforms were introduced.

Q157.label: François Hollande
Q157.summary: François Gérard Georges Nicolas Hollande is a French politician who served as President of France from 2012 to 2017. Before his presidency, he was First Secretary of the Socialist Party (PS) from 1997 to 2008, Mayor of Tulle from 2001 to 2008, as well as President of the General Council of Corrèze from 2008 to 2012.

Q1708189.label: 2008 Monegasque general election
Q1708189.summary: General elections were held in Monaco on 3 February 2008. The Union for Monaco was re-elected, though with a reduced margin of victory.

Q65121437.label: November 2019 Spanish general election
Q65121437.desc: election of Congress and most Senate seats
Q65121437.summary: A general election was held in Spain on 10 November 2019 to elect the members of the 14th Cortes Generales under the Spanish Constitution of 1978. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election, as well as 208 of 265 seats in the Senate.

Q121518237.label: 2023 Polish referendum
Q121518237.summary: A referendum was held in Poland on 15 October 2023, taking place alongside the nationwide elections to the Senate and Sejm.

Q3722397.label: 1993 Serbian parliamentary election
Q3722397.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the Yugoslav republic of Serbia on 19 December 1993, to elect members of the National Assembly. The Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) of Slobodan Milošević emerged as the largest party in the National Assembly, winning 123 of the 250 seats.

Q18547357.label: Romanian constitutional referendum, 2003
Q18547357.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Romania on 18 and 19 October 2003. The proposed amendments to the constitution were approved by 91.1% of voters.

Q6497437.label: Latvian citizenship referendum, 1927
Q6497437.desc: a referendum on the citizenship law, held in Latvia on 17 and 18 December 1927
Q6497437.summary: A referendum on the citizenship law was held in Latvia on 17 and 18 December 1927. Voters were asked whether they approved of repealing the amendments made to the citizenship law by the Saeima. The referendum was passed and the amendments were cancelled. Of a total of 1,120,026 registered voters, only 242,798 cast valid votes.

Q20182173.label: 2016 Lithuanian parliamentary election
Q20182173.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Lithuania on 9 and 23 October 2016 to elect the 141 members of the Seimas. 71 were elected in single-member constituencies using the two-round system, and the remaining 70 in a single nationwide constituency using proportional representation. The first round was held on 9 October and the second round on 23 October.

Q1966237.label: 1998 Danish general election
Q1966237.summary: General elections were held in Denmark on 11 March 1998. Although the centre-right parties led by Venstre had been expected to win, the Social Democratic Party-led government of Poul Nyrup Rasmussen remained in power in a very close vote that required several recounts.

Q315549.label: Kuniaki Koiso
Q315549.summary: Kuniaki Koiso was a Japanese politician and general who served as prime minister of Japan from 1944 to 1945, during World War II. He previously served as minister of colonial affairs in 1939 and 1940, and as governor-general of Korea from 1942 to 1944. Koiso resigned as premier after the start of the Battle of Okinawa, and following Japan's surrender he was convicted as a Class A war criminal and sentenced to life imprisonment, dying in prison in 1950.

Q3077789.label: epidemiology of HIV/AIDS
Q3077789.summary: The global pandemic of HIV/AIDS began in 1981, and is an ongoing worldwide public health issue. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), by 2023, HIV/AIDS had killed approximately 40.4 million people, and approximately 39 million people were infected with HIV globally. Of these, 29.8 million people (75%) are receiving antiretroviral treatment.

Q20977821.label: 2015 Burkinabé coup d'état attempt
Q20977821.img: RSP soldiers during the 2015 Burkinabé coup.png
Q20977821.summary: The 2015 Burkina Faso coup attempt was a failed coup d'état launched on 16 September 2015 in Burkina Faso, when members of the Regiment of Presidential Security (RSP) – a controversial autonomous military unit, formed under President Blaise Compaoré – detained the country's government.

mentions.c: Burkina Faso: Coup: 2015 Burkinabé coup d'état attempt

Q42103453.label: Battle of Kirkuk
Q42103453.summary: The Battle of Kirkuk, codenamed Operation Enforcing Security of the 2017 Iraqi–Kurdish conflict, was a military deployment by the Iraqi Security Forces to retake Kirkuk Governorate from the Peshmerga after the latter ignored repeated warnings to withdraw, sparking clashes between the two forces.

Q41117.label: Kim Il-sung
Q41117.desc: Supreme Leader of North Korea from 1948 to 1994
Q41117.summary: Kim Il Sung was a North Korean communist revolutionary, military officer, politician, and dictator who founded the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), also known as North Korea, in 1948, and led it until his death in 1994. He was succeeded by his son Kim Jong Il and posthumously declared Eternal President. He was the third-longest serving non-royal head of state and government in the 20th century, in office for more than 45 years.
